features.name: Data transfer
features.description: A feature that enables efficient bulk data movement by bypassing AL's abstraction layer and directly leveraging SQL's native capabilities. Allows developers to transfer large datasets at significantly higher performance than looping through records.
caveats: Requires manual code changes to adopt
Only works against SQL, not temporary tables or CRM
Most beneficial with large tables, minimal impact on small datasets

features.name: Set load fields (partial records)
features.description: A language feature that allows developers to specify which fields to load from a table, reducing the amount of data retrieved from SQL and improving query performance. Automatically applied to API pages. Allows selective loading of fields from tables to remove joins in SQL queries. Most relevant for performance-critical code looping through millions of rows.
caveats: Requires manual code changes for non-API scenarios
Impact reduced after extension table consolidation from multiple extension tables to single companion table
Most effective in performance-critical code with large row counts
Less important after removal of many table extensions in favor of one
Best used in performance-critical code scenarios

features.name: Read isolation
features.description: A fine-grained control feature that allows developers to specify SQL isolation semantics when reading data, providing options beyond the traditional read committed or read uncommitted choices. Offers four isolation levels: read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, and update lock. Allows developers to specify desired isolation level in code.
caveats: Newer feature compared to data transfer and set load fields
Developed alongside tri-state locking feature
Requires developers to specify isolation level in code
Adds complexity despite abstraction of SQL details

features.name: Tri-state locking
features.description: Companion feature to read isolation that adds a third locking state between read uncommitted and update lock. After a modification, subsequent reads use read committed instead of update lock, allowing sessions to read each other's data without blocking.
caveats: Was initially opt-in but now enabled by default
Can still be disabled with lock table
Hard to measure telemetry impact due to adoption trajectory

features.name: Many table extensions to one optimization
features.description: Automatic optimization that consolidates multiple table extensions into a single one. Required no code changes from customers, only an upgrade to the next major version.
caveats: Happened automatically during upgrade
No developer action required

features.name: Lock table function behavior
features.description: Contrary to its name, lock table does not immediately lock the entire table in SQL. Instead, it sets all future reads to use update lock hints and affects the data cache. This is a common misconception about the function's actual behavior.
caveats: Function name is misleading about actual behavior
Named 20 years ago with outdated naming

features.name: Set current key function behavior
features.description: Contrary to expectations, set current key does not instruct SQL to use a specific index. Instead, it orders the resulting data in the specified field order, which can have significant SQL optimization implications as SQL may choose different indexes or sort data after retrieval.
caveats: Name does not suggest actual behavior
Difficult to rename due to backward compatibility
Can cause SQL to choose suboptimal query plans

features.name: Temporary tables
features.description: In-memory tables implemented using AVL tree data structure within the NST process memory. Fast due to in-memory operation with transparent abstraction, but memory consumption scales with data volume.
caveats: Memory usage increases with data volume
Implementation not well documented

features.name: Dynamic queries at runtime
features.description: Ability to create queries at runtime instead of design time, allowing dynamic joins and conditional logic based on record values or conditions. Would enable runtime construction of queries instead of design-time definition with conditional joins and dynamic composition of query structure based on runtime conditions.
caveats: Still at idea level, not yet in code
Design of syntax not yet finalized
Challenge to make succinct without too much boilerplate
Would require finding a succinct way to describe queries
Needs ability to generate queries on the fly
Challenge in making the model not cumbersome to write

features.name: Query builder pattern for queries
features.description: Proposed approach to make dynamic queries more succinct by allowing developers to chain data items, joins, and fields together rather than writing traditional query objects.
caveats: Conceptual idea still being explored
Challenge to make it succinct without cumbersome code
May rely on composition patterns

features.name: AI-powered query generation via MCP server
features.description: Concept to use MCP servers and AI that understands table metadata to generate queries on the fly, potentially from natural language descriptions.
caveats: Very recently discussed
Needs dynamic query generation ability first
Experimental approach planned for MCP before AO

features.name: Bulk events for delete and modify
features.description: Event model that fires once for bulk operations instead of once per row, allowing subscriptions to bulk delete or bulk modify with filter information instead of individual row events.
caveats: Big change to AL needed
Currently falls back to row-by-row when row triggers exist
Requires shifting away from row-by-row mental model

features.name: Move towards set-based operations
features.description: Long-term goal to shift AL from row-by-row processing toward SQL set-based operations, potentially inspired by LINQ patterns from C#.
caveats: Probably quite a big change to AL
Long-term vision, not near-term
Would require significant runtime evolution

features.name: Sampling profiler tool
features.description: Profiler tool available for identifying hot path code and performance bottlenecks by sampling code execution.
caveats: Requires developer analysis to use effectively
Results vary by scenario

features.name: Dictionary data type for optimization
features.description: Dictionary data type that can replace temporary tables in some cases, offering constant-time lookup versus logarithmic time of temporary tables.
caveats: Only applicable in lookup scenarios
Not suitable when table structure needed
Best for quick value lookups
